messages.subject: breedR v0.11
messages.body_plain:
Dear breedRs,

I have just made a major release <https://github.com/famuvie/breedR/releases/tag/v0.11> of breedR.

Nothing important has changed from the latest version 0.10-22.
I cleaned up several minor bugs and documentation issues.

This simply closes the v0.10 series, where all the high priority issues were addressed, like the computation of heritability, and the installation process.

More importantly, it start the v0.11 series, where I will start implementing the multi-trait support.

Remember that now the installation has been greatly simplified, and you can update breedR as a regular package avoiding the heavy devtools. For that you only need to add the new breedR repository to your list of package repositories (check getOption(“repos”)). Follow the instructions on the breedR site <http://famuvie.github.io/breedR/>.

Have a good weekend
ƒacu.-
​

messages.subject: breedR workshop materials
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I have just gathered all the materials from the workshop last week in
Warsaw, and set up a webpage
<http://famuvie.github.io/breedR/workshop_IBL/> on the breedR’s website
<http://famuvie.github.io/breedR>.

You will find either individual links to the slides and code for each of
the sessions, or you can also download all the material together
<http://famuvie.github.io/breedR/workshop_IBL/breedR_IBL.zip> in a
compressed file.

A couple of notes though.

 1.

    The material for the breedR Overview was taken literally from the
    vignette, which you can find either in the package or in the wiki.
    Hence I did not include these slides, just links, where you will
    always find the most recent version.

 2.

    Some of the slides are in html format and require an internet
    connection to display correctly.
    You can find a standalone copy for local off-line visualization in
    the compressed materials.

Happy breeding
ƒacu.-

​
--
